name: Sigulda Medieval Castle

opening_hours.seasonal_note: Park grounds freely accessible at all times. Museum and tower have seasonal hours.

tagline: The Livonian Order's first Latvian stronghold in the Gauja valley
highlights: Picturesque ruins with intact gate tower and curtain wall
Directly beside the 19th-century Sigulda New Castle (now a conference centre)
Gateway to the Gauja National Park valley excursions

description: Sigulda Medieval Castle is the oldest Livonian Order castle in Latvia, founded in 1207 as the first permanent stronghold of the crusading Order of the Brethren of the Sword. Standing at the edge of the Gauja river gorge, the ruins preserve a striking gate tower, sections of curtain wall, and the foundations of the great hall, now framed by mature trees within a public park. Adjacent to the ruins stands the 19th-century Sigulda New Castle, a neo-Gothic manor built by Prince Kropotkin that today serves as the municipal government building and a wedding venue. Together with Turaida and Krimulda castles across the gorge, Sigulda's medieval ruins form the centrepiece of the Gauja National Park heritage trail — Latvia's most popular outdoor excursion.
history:
The Livonian Brothers of the Sword established Sigulda Castle in 1207 as their first permanent stronghold in Latvia — the operational base from which the crusading Order extended its campaigns into Latvian and Estonian territory and consolidated its grip on the Gauja River valley. Expansion through the 13th and 14th centuries developed the castle into a substantial fortified complex at the edge of the Gauja gorge, one of the most strategically placed positions in medieval Livonia.

The Livonian Wars of the 16th century brought damage that the castle did not recover from, and it was gradually abandoned, falling into the ruin that now occupies the headland above the gorge. The adjacent New Castle was built in 1878 for Prince Dmitry Kropotkin — a 19th-century manor house built in sight of the medieval ruins that had preceded it — and serves today as the administrative headquarters of Sigulda town.

The ruins were preserved as a heritage site and park through the 20th century and remain the centrepiece of the Gauja National Park landscape, with the gorge, the cable car, and the Turaida Museum Reserve visible across the valley.
how_to_visit:
**Getting there:** Sigulda is 50 km from Riga — trains run hourly from Riga Central Station (1 hour). The castle ruins are a 15-minute walk from Sigulda train station, making this one of Latvia's most accessible castle visits without a car.

**Tickets:** €3 adult / €1 child for the ruins and museum tower (park grounds are freely accessible at all times). The GYG Sigulda & Turaida Day Tour from Riga (t608853, from €99, 4.9★/118 reviews) is a 6-hour circuit covering both Sigulda and Turaida Castles with a guide.

**Practical tips:** The ruins are best seen in about 1 hour, but allow extra time to walk to the gorge viewpoint and to use the cable car across the Gauja valley to Krimulda on the opposite bank — the view from the cable car across the forested gorge with Turaida's red-brick tower visible opposite is Sigulda's signature image. The bobsled track and bungee platform are also on-site if activity tourism interests you.

**Combine with:** [Turaida Castle](/castles/latvia/turaida-castle), visible across the gorge, is the essential second stop — Latvia's most complete Livonian castle with a full museum reserve, accessible via the valley trails or cable car. [Cēsis Castle](/castles/latvia/cesis-castle), 30 km north, completes the Gauja Valley medieval castle circuit.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Sigulda Castle and Turaida Castle?
faqs.answer: Sigulda was built by the Livonian Order (military crusaders) while Turaida was built by the Archbishop of Riga. Sigulda is largely ruined; Turaida has a restored tower and a full museum reserve.

faqs.question: Can I cross the gorge to Turaida?
faqs.answer: Yes — a cable car runs across the Gauja gorge from near Sigulda Castle to Krimulda on the other side, and walking trails connect the valley sites.

faqs.question: Is the New Castle open to visit?
faqs.answer: The exterior can be freely viewed. The interior serves as a conference and events venue, so interior visits are limited to scheduled events.
